proposed_from.topic: Boundary-complete proxy-cycle target rigidity for selected probabilities of causation. In the exact finite Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki four-response-type model with binary treatment and outcome, finite proxies, latent confounding, outcome-dependent selection, positive observed selected tables, and nonnegative latent proxy mechanisms, define the full normalized response-cycle factorization fiber. Treat separately the two-proxy design with supplied positive population cell margins and the relevant-IV design with unknown margins and shared-Z equations. Prove an observable rank/support/cycle criterion that is necessary and sufficient for PN/PS constancy on every nonempty mixed-rank and boundary fiber. Emit rational formulas where possible and exact algebraic certificates otherwise; on every nonrigid stratum emit two legal full SCMs with identical observables and margins but different targets, requiring strict-positive twins only in interior strata. Prove termination and fixed-alphabet exact output bounds, stable Wald inference on separated rigid strata, and multinomial confidence-fiber inversion near rank/support transitions. Apply the atlas to the GEUVADIS SWAP70-to-SBF2-AS1 selected-expression analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the full nonnegative cycle-to-SCM lift, a complete all-rank-two orientation-box atlas including an identified assignment boundary, the stacked-rank-four affine-annihilation branch, and an exact relevant-IV residual-ratio/forest reduction with one cycle-product constraint. A complete mixed chart yields a cubic nuisance root and legal target-changing completions; fourteen mixed two-proxy and eight unknown-margin IV instances were checked exactly. Forced-zero boundaries, coincident lines, inactive rows, hidden Z splits, cross-face comparisons, and current NMF/counterfactual collisions were tested. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove explicit mixed-support cycle target elimination across every real component and support face, with target agreement tests or legal twin extraction, without reducing the classification to generic two-copy quantifier elimination. EARLY KILL TEST: Compile the residual-ratio/forest rules for ternary inactive-row and coincident-endpoint patterns and compare them with exact full-fiber elimination on independently sampled rational observable tables; any missed target-varying component kills the classifier, while an irrational singleton must use the authorized exact-algebraic branch. seed_details.title: Joint two-design rigidity atlas
seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 1, Corollary 1, equations (10)--(14), Appendix equations (A.21)--(A.33), the Introduction, and the Discussion were inspected in the publisher PDF.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor identifies proxy endpoints by determinant ratios and inverse matrices. Those operations stop deciding the target when a cell has rank one, endpoints coincide, an incident coefficient vanishes, or shared-instrument equations leave unknown margin scales.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the inversions in equations (A.28)--(A.31) by support-face charts, oriented rank-two segments, rank-one endpoint transfers, and a residual-ratio forest around the response cycle.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches through September 2026 for selected PN/PS, proxy-cycle rigidity, target-specific NMF identification, and nonnegative support geometry found factor-uniqueness results but no necessary-and-sufficient target atlas for this selected response cycle.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki because their determinant formulas already identify PN and PS whenever identification is possible.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their conditions are sufficient and explicitly invertible; the anchor proof does not analyze singular or forced-zero fibers, and the presolve contains both rigid boundary examples outside those conditions and target-changing fibers with the same observables.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not a do-calculus relabeling: the focal object is a finite observable rank/support/cycle compiler with an if-and-only-if target criterion, legal global witnesses, exact encodings, and an inference rung.

seed_details.title: Boundary-complete two-proxy rigidity
seed_details.anchor_opened: The two-proxy setup in Section 3.1 and the endpoint-recovery proof in Appendix A were read together with the Introduction and Discussion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The supplied-margin full fiber remains meaningful after observable rank loss, but the anchor's inverse construction provides neither necessity nor cross-face target comparison.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace each regular endpoint intersection by the complete product of oriented segment intervals and mixed rank-one incidence charts.
seed_details.destination_search: Rank-two NMF segment geometry is occupied, but searches found no labeled-cycle theorem characterizing constancy of only the two causal barycentric weights on every support face.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from the rank-two nested-polytope characterization because every cell factorization is just a segment.
seed_details.rebuttal: Individual segment descriptions do not glue the four shared latent endpoints, inactive rows, and cross-face target values; the cycle-level necessity and legal twin extraction are additional global statements.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is an effect-rigidity theorem over a selected SCM fiber, not full NMF uniqueness.

seed_details.title: Unknown-margin relevant-IV forest atlas
seed_details.anchor_opened: Corollary 1, equation (13), the population independence equation (14), Appendix B, and the Introduction and Discussion were inspected.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor uses regular equations for population margins, whereas response-type IV exogeneity couples all four cells and leaves projective scales on inactive residual components.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Subtract a projective baseline from each shared-\(Z\) equation, convert nonzero residual pairs into signed margin ratios, and close ratios only on active cycles while retaining forest component scales.
seed_details.destination_search: The nearest finite-response IV paper and nonunique-bridge paper do not classify inactive rows, coincident endpoints, residual forests, or target constancy across real components.
seed_details.referee_objection: Equation (14) and standard polynomial elimination already decide the unknown margins.
seed_details.rebuttal: Equation (14) is only a population independence consequence and does not enforce response-level common-\(Z\) equations; generic elimination also supplies neither an observable structural criterion nor cycle-specific certificates.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names the residual-ratio forest and cycle product as focal objects and requires necessity, not only an IV sufficient condition.

seed_details.title: Sharp PN/PS images of nonrigid fibers
seed_details.anchor_opened: The response-function linear program, Theorems 1--4, the sharpness construction, the Introduction, and the Conclusion were read in the archival paper.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Tian--Pearl obtain sharp closed-form bounds from a response-type polytope. Selection and proxy cycles replace that polytope by a possibly disconnected bilinear semialgebraic fiber.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace dual-polytope vertex enumeration by support-chart target-image elimination and endpoint-attaining SCM lifts on every real component.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches located selection-aware risk-difference bounds and proxy-effect bounds, but no sharp selected PN/PS image theorem with coupled proxy cycles and unknown margins.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate by optimizing PN and PS over the finite response-type probabilities as in Tian--Pearl.
seed_details.rebuttal: The selected proxy constraints are bilinear factorization and cycle equations, so the feasible set is not the Tian--Pearl polytope and can have disconnected algebraic components with irrational endpoints.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This seed uses graphical compatible-SCM bounds and exact algebraic target images, not an unspecified LP.

seed_details.title: Confidence-fiber inference across identification transitions
seed_details.anchor_opened: The identification discussion, Theorems 2.1--2.2 and 3.4, influence function (19), the efficiency appendix, the Introduction, and the Discussion were read in the arXiv manuscript.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Zhang et al. regularize a nonunique linear bridge solution set, but a proxy-cycle target can jump from smooth point identification to a set across rank and support discriminants.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace canonical bridge selection by inversion of a simultaneous multinomial observable-law region through the full legal SCM correspondence, while retaining a smooth-chart delta method away from the discriminant.
seed_details.destination_search: Weak-identification conditional tests, stable counterfactual-bound inference, and exact contingency-table confidence sequences do not project through a changing selected proxy-cycle fiber.
seed_details.referee_objection: Coverage is immediate by projecting any multinomial confidence region and therefore has no statistical content.
seed_details.rebuttal: Containment gives the coverage backbone, but the research content is a computable exact fiber inversion that agrees with efficient Wald inference on separated charts and remains valid under local rank/support transitions.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The inference layer modifies a necessary-and-sufficient identification shape; it is not labeled as bare M8.

seed_details.title: Critical violation radius for proxy exclusion
seed_details.anchor_opened: The categorical matrix formula (5), continuous bridge Theorem 1, rank-failure test Theorem 2, the Introduction, and the Discussion were read in the Biometrika manuscript.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Miao et al. identify an average causal effect under exact proxy independences and a rank condition but do not quantify how selected PN/PS changes under bounded violations of the proxy exclusion.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Relax each proxy conditional-independence equality by an observable total-variation radius and eliminate the perturbed cycle to derive the first radius at which zero enters the PN or PS set.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found many invalid-proxy average-effect methods but no critical-radius theorem for selected probabilities of causation.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a routine sensitivity analysis once the exact fiber is written down.
seed_details.rebuttal: A critical radius would require sharp optimization over a nonconvex selected response-cycle fiber and cannot be obtained by perturbing the anchor's inverse formula near singular strata.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names a critical scalar and sharp bounds, but it is deferred because it expands the model before the exact zero-radius atlas is complete.

seed_details.title: Minimal proxy alphabet for generic target identification
seed_details.anchor_opened: The categorical rank argument, formula (5), and rank-failure discussion were read together with the Introduction and Discussion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The rank condition links proxy alphabet size to latent support for average effects, suggesting an analogous minimal-design question for four response types.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the square proxy operator rank count by the labeled response-cycle incidence dimension and solve for the smallest \((|\mathcal W|,|\mathcal Z|)\) admitting generic PN/PS rigidity.
seed_details.destination_search: Generic latent-class dimension results already characterize many alphabet thresholds, and the target-specific improvement was not supported by a concrete boundary mechanism.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from generic latent-class dimension counting and Kruskal-type identifiability.
seed_details.rebuttal: No adequate rebuttal survived: without a target-specific strict improvement, the result would be a design corollary rather than a new kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The candidate collapses to a generic-identifiability restatement.

seed_details.title: Linear annihilator characterization of target rigidity
seed_details.anchor_opened: The nonunique bridge identification argument, solution-set estimator, influence function theorem, and Discussion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: A linear causal functional can annihilate the null space of a bridge operator even when the bridge is nonunique. The proxy-cycle analogue is nonlinear and face-dependent.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Intersect target annihilation of the factorization rigidity cone with global component agreement and shared-instrument residual equations.
seed_details.destination_search: NMF rigidity papers treat factor uniqueness, while proximal papers treat linear bridge operators; neither gives a global nonlinear target-annihilator criterion for this four-cycle.
seed_details.referee_objection: Immediate from checking whether the target gradient annihilates the tangent space.
seed_details.rebuttal: Tangent annihilation is only local and misses one-sided boundary motions, disconnected components, and different support faces with distinct constant target values.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The required global-component comparison prevents the seed from being a merely infinitesimal rigidity test.

seed_details.title: GEUVADIS model-to-data certification
seed_details.anchor_opened: Section 5, Table 1, the variable mapping, the imposed selection probabilities, and the paper's Introduction and Discussion were read.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The application assumes the IV and proxy graph and applies regular formulas, while its broad bootstrap ranges reach both logical boundaries and do not certify the model or identification stratum.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace plug-in evaluation under assumed Conditions 2--3 by exact compatibility, atlas placement, and confidence-fiber projection using the released contingency counts.
seed_details.destination_search: The GEUVADIS and MRPC sources discuss causal orientation and replication but do not provide a selected PN/PS factorization certificate.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is only a diagnostic reanalysis of one public data set.
seed_details.rebuttal: The audit is a concrete consumer and falsification target for the atlas, but it is not retained as the theorem kernel by itself.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The application is explicitly secondary to the general identification theorem.
